# Planner — Progress Memory

> **This file is the agent's persistent memory.** The `Planner` agent
> (`.github/agents/planner.agent.md`) MUST read this at session start and update it at session
> end. Keep it accurate and current. Commit it together with the work it describes.

## Mission

Turn each changelog feature (from the Changelog Researcher's backlog) into a concrete,
step-by-step implementation plan for the `llm` VS Code extension. The planner does NOT write
code — only the Coder writes code.

## Active plan — 1.101-6 · Chat UX improvements (distinct user messages, visible undo, navigable attachments)

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — user messages visually distinct from AI responses; undoing a request is visible (hover X button or ⌘Backspace); attachments from the input box are more navigable. Relevance: keep (capability/context) — chat UX. Gap: webview renders messages but per-request undo is not implemented; user styling is minimal; attachment strip is a bare thumbnail row.
- **Approach:** Three orthogonal UX features, all in the single webview + host pair. (1) **Distinct user messages:** strengthen the existing `.message.user` styling (accent left border + bolder label) and give every user message a stable `data-idx` (its index in the host `history` array at render time) so the webview can address it for undo. (2) **Visible undo:** a hover `×` button (`.msg-undo`, same pattern as the existing `.copy-btn` on assistant messages) on every user message posts `{ type: 'undo_request', index }` to the host; the host truncates `this.history` to `index` (drops that user turn AND all following turns — "undo a request and all following") and posts `{ type: 'undo_done', messages, conversations, activeId }`; the webview re-renders the message list from `messages` (reusing the existing `restore` render path). ⌘Backspace (and Ctrl+Backspace) in the webview posts the same `undo_request` with the LAST user message's index. No-op when streaming or when there is no user message to undo. (3) **Navigable attachments:** the pending-image strip (`#attach-strip`) becomes horizontally scrollable with a count label; the attach button shows a pending-count badge; clicking a pending thumbnail opens a full-size lightbox preview (click backdrop to close); clicking a sent message image (`.msg-img`) opens the same lightbox.
- **Files to touch:** `src/chat/webview.ts`, `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/chat/webview.ts` (1 file, webview-only, no host changes): (a) CSS: `.message.user .content` gains `border-left: 2px solid var(--focus)` (keep existing `--user-bg` background); `.message.user .role` gains `color: var(--fg)`; new `.msg-undo` rule cloned from `.copy-btn` (opacity 0 → 1 on `.message.user:hover`); `#attach-strip` gains `overflow-x: auto; max-width: 100%` + `::-webkit-scrollbar` thin styling; new `.attach-count` (11px muted label) and `.attach-badge` (small rounded count chip on `#attach`); new `#lightbox` (fixed, full-viewport, `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` backdrop, centered `img` max 90vw/90vh, `cursor: zoom-out`). (b) `window.addUserMessage(text, images, idx)` — new optional 3rd param; sets `el.dataset.idx = String(idx ?? '')`; appends a `<button class="msg-undo" title="Undo this request and everything after it">×</button>` inside the `.role` div (role div becomes flex like assistant's); click handler posts `{ type: 'undo_request', index: Number(el.dataset.idx) }` when `idx` is a valid number and `!streaming`. (c) `renderAttachStrip()` — prepend a `.attach-count` span (`N pending`) when `pendingImages.length > 0`; update `#attach` badge text/visibility; each thumbnail `im` gets `cursor: zoom-in` + click → `openLightbox(img.dataUrl)`. (d) New `openLightbox(dataUrl)` / `closeLightbox()` — create/reuse a single `#lightbox` element with an `<img>`; backdrop click or `Esc` closes. (e) In the `restore` render loop, pass the user message's array index as `idx` to `addUserMessage`. (f) `keydown` listener on `document`: `e.key === 'Backspace' && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey)` → `e.preventDefault()`, find the last `.message.user` with a numeric `data-idx`, post `{ type: 'undo_request', index }` (only when `!streaming`). (g) `.msg-img` (sent message images) get `cursor: zoom-in` + click → `openLightbox`. Compiles standalone: pure webview string changes, no TS API surface change.
  - **S-002** — `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts` (1 file): (a) `WebviewToHostMessage` handling: new `case "undo_request"` in the webview→host switch — read `index` (integer 0 ≤ index < history.length, else ignore); if `this.abortController` is active → post `{ type: 'error', message: 'Stop the running request first.' }` and return; else `this.history = this.history.slice(0, index)`; `this.preRunHistory = null` (stale checkpoint after truncation); `this.pushHistory()` (existing method posts `restore` with `messages` + `conversations` + `activeId` — the webview's existing `restore` case re-renders everything, so no new host→webview message type is needed); post `{ type: 'undo_done' }` as a lightweight confirmation (webview may ignore it). (b) Guard: undo while a conversation is persisted → the existing `pushHistory`/persist path already saves the truncated history. Compiles standalone: only adds a switch case + uses existing `pushHistory`.
  - **S-003** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new named guards (static source checks on `src/chat/webview.ts` + `src/chat/ChatViewProvider.ts`, matching the established pattern for webview items): (1) `webview.ts` contains `.msg-undo` CSS + `undo_request` postMessage; (2) `addUserMessage` signature includes `idx` and sets `data-idx`; (3) `undo_request` case exists in `ChatViewProvider.ts` and truncates via `this.history.slice(0, index)`; (4) undo guard: `abortController` check present before truncation; (5) ⌘Backspace handler present (`Backspace` + `metaKey || ctrlKey` + `preventDefault`); (6) `#attach-strip` CSS has `overflow-x: auto`; (7) `.attach-count` and `.attach-badge` present; (8) `openLightbox`/`closeLightbox` defined and wired to both pending thumbnails and `.msg-img`; (9) `restore` render loop passes the index to `addUserMessage`; (10) `undo_request` with out-of-range index is a no-op (source check: bounds check `index < this.history.length`). Gate **870 → 880** (+10).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** `npm run compile` exit 0; smoke 880/880; user messages render with the accent left border + full-strength "You" label and a hover `×` undo button; clicking the `×` (or ⌘Backspace) truncates the host history to before that user turn (the turn and all following turns are gone from both the panel and the persisted conversation); undo is a no-op while a request is streaming (error posted) and when no user message exists; the pending-attachment strip scrolls horizontally, shows a count label and a badge on the attach button, and clicking any thumbnail (pending or sent) opens a full-size lightbox that closes on backdrop click or Esc; no new npm dependencies; assistant-message rendering, retry, and all existing webview behavior unchanged.
- **Risks:** `data-idx` is positional — after a host-side truncation the webview is fully re-rendered via `restore`, so indices stay consistent (no incremental DOM patching); ⌘Backspace is intercepted only in the webview (no VS Code command registered — keeps scope minimal and matches "visible in the chat"); undoing drops the `preRunHistory` checkpoint (documented: file-change undo is tied to the last run, which no longer exists after the request is undone); lightbox is a single shared element (no stacking of multiple previews).
- **Next item:** (none recorded — 1.101-6 is the last item of the current user goal; confirm with orchestrator).

## Done plan — 1.101-5 · MCP development mode (VS Code 1.101)

- **Status:** Planned — 2026-10-24 (built + verified PASS, tag `changelog-1.101-5`)
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.101 — add a `dev` key to the MCP server config: `watch` (file glob to restart the server on change) and `debug` (attach a debugger; Node.js and Python). Relevance: keep (capability/context) — MCP dev UX. Gap: no dev mode. Extend: parse `dev.watch` glob, watch for changes, restart the server process; `dev.debug` launches with `--inspect` (node) or `debugpy` (python).
- **Approach:** Two orthogonal, minimal features, both stdio-only (HTTP servers have no process to watch/debug — `dev` is ignored for `url` servers). (1) **`dev.debug`** is pure spawn-arg rewriting: a pure helper `mcpDebugArgs(command, args, debug)` in `src/mcp.ts` returns the args to spawn with — Node runtime (`node`/`nodejs` basename) → insert `--inspect` as the first arg after the command; Python runtime (`python`/`python2`/`python3` basename) → prepend `-m debugpy --listen 5678` before the existing args; unknown runtime → args unchanged. `McpManager.ensureStarted` computes `cfg.dev?.debug ? mcpDebugArgs(...) : cfg.args` and passes the result via a shallow-copied config to `new McpClient(...)` — `McpClient` itself is untouched (it already spawns `config.command` with `config.args`). No VS Code Debug API: "attach" means the server listens on the inspect port; the user attaches externally. (2) **`dev.watch`** is a directory-level `fs.watch` (no `chokidar`): a pure helper `mcpWatchTarget(glob)` in `src/mcp.ts` returns `{ dir, match }` where `dir` is the longest literal prefix of the glob before the first wildcard (relative globs resolve against `process.cwd()`; empty prefix → `.`) and `match` is a RegExp built from the glob (`**/` → `.*`, `*` → `[^/]*`, `?` → `[^/]`, everything else escaped; anchored full-string match against the changed file's path relative to `dir`). `McpManager` owns the watcher lifecycle: `private devWatchers = new Map<string, { watcher: FSWatcher; timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined }>()`; after a successful `ensureStarted` (only when `cfg.dev?.watch` is a non-empty string AND the server is stdio), `startDevWatch(name)` calls `fs.watch(dir, { persistent: false })` and on each event (debounced 500 ms, timer `unref`'d) checks `match.test(path)` and, on a hit, calls the existing `this.refresh(name)` (close + restart — never throws, records status). `setServers` stops the watcher for removed servers; `dispose()` stops all watchers and clears the map. Watcher failures (bad dir, EACCES) are swallowed with a `notify` message — dev mode must never break server startup.
- **Files to touch:** `src/mcp.ts`, `src/mcpManager.ts`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices:**
  - **S-001** — `src/mcp.ts` (1 file, pure types + helpers, no `vscode` import): `McpDevConfig` interface (`watch?: string; debug?: boolean`); `McpServerConfig` += `dev?: McpDevConfig`; `parseMcpServers` — coerce `entry.dev` (plain object only; `watch` kept only when a non-empty string; `debug` kept only when a boolean; if neither survives, `dev` stays `undefined`); `mcpWatchTarget(glob: string): { dir: string; match: RegExp }` (pure, per the glob rules above; throws `invalid watch glob` on empty/whitespace input); `mcpDebugArgs(command: string, args: string[], debug: boolean): string[]` (pure; `debug` false/absent → `args` unchanged; Node/Python rules above; returns a NEW array, never mutates input).
  - **S-002** — `src/mcpManager.ts` (1 file): import `fs` (`watch`, `FSWatcher`) + `mcpDebugArgs`, `mcpWatchTarget` from `./mcp`; `McpManager` += `private devWatchers = new Map<string, { watcher: FSWatcher; timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined }>()`; `ensureStarted` — when constructing a stdio client, compute `const spawnArgs = cfg.dev?.debug ? mcpDebugArgs(cfg.command!, cfg.args ?? [], true) : cfg.args` and pass `{ ...cfg, args: spawnArgs }` to `new McpClient(...)`; after a successful start, if `cfg.dev?.watch` is set and the server is stdio → `this.startDevWatch(name, cfg.dev.watch)`; `private startDevWatch(name, glob)` — try `mcpWatchTarget(glob)` (catch → `notify` + return), `fs.watch(dir, { persistent: false })`; on event: 500 ms debounce (clear + reset timer, `unref`'d), then if `match.test(eventPath)` → `void this.refresh(name)`; store `{ watcher, timer }` in `devWatchers`; watcher `error` event → `notify` + `stopDevWatch(name)`; `private stopDevWatch(name)` — clear timer, `watcher.close()`, delete map entry (idempotent); `setServers` — for each removed server also call `stopDevWatch(name)`; `dispose()` — `stopDevWatch` for every entry + clear the map.
  - **S-003** — `scripts/smoke-test.js` (1 file): new assertions — `mcpWatchTarget` (literal dir extraction: `./src/**/*.py` → dir `./src`, `**/*.js` → dir `.`; regex behavior: `**/*.py` matches `a/b/c.py` and `c.py` but not `c.ts`; `*` does not cross `/`; empty glob throws); `mcpDebugArgs` (node + `--inspect` inserted first; python3 → `-m debugpy --listen 5678` prepended before existing args; unknown command → unchanged; `debug: false` → unchanged; input array not mutated); `parseMcpServers` dev coercion (valid `dev` kept; `dev.watch` non-string dropped; `dev.debug` non-boolean dropped; all-invalid `dev` → `undefined`; `dev` on a `url` server still parsed but harmless); `McpManager` dev wiring via a fake stdio server (spawn a `node -e` echo-MCP stub): `dev.debug: true` → spawned process args include `--inspect` (assert via the stub printing its `process.argv` on stderr, or via a config-level static source check that `ensureStarted` passes the rewritten args); `dev.watch` → `fs.watch` invoked on the resolved dir (stub `fs.watch` in the smoke test to capture the dir + simulate an event → assert `refresh`-equivalent restart happened: server status returns to `running` with a fresh client); removed server via `setServers` → watcher stopped (stub `close` called); `dispose` → all watchers closed. Static source check: `mcpManager.ts` imports `mcpDebugArgs`/`mcpWatchTarget` and `fs`. Gate **858 → 870** (+12).
- **Acceptance criteria (whole item):** compile passes; smoke 870/870; a stdio server configured with `dev.debug: true` spawns with `--inspect` (node) or `-m debugpy --listen 5678` (python) and completes the normal handshake; a stdio server with `dev.watch: "<glob>"` restarts (close + re-handshake, status back to `running`) when a matching file changes and does NOT restart on non-matching changes; removing the server from config or disposing the manager stops all watchers (no leaked handles — `persistent: false` + explicit close); servers without `dev` and all HTTP servers behave exactly as before; no new deps.
- **Risks:** `fs.watch` is directory-level and platform-behavior varies (macOS FSEvents coalesces; Linux inotify is per-file but `fs.watch` on a dir reports child changes) — the 500 ms debounce + glob re-match keeps it correct at the cost of a small delay; a glob whose literal prefix does not exist yet → `fs.watch` throws → swallowed with a `notify` (documented: create the dir first); `dev.watch` on a `url` server is silently ignored (no process to restart) — documented; `debugpy` must already be installed in the Python environment (we only add launch args, never install) — documented; `--inspect` port 9229 / debugpy port 5678 are fixed defaults (no port config in this item — matches "keep it minimal"); concurrent watch-triggered restarts are serialized by the existing `starting` dedupe in `ensureStarted` (a restart while a start is in flight reuses the in-flight promise — acceptable); the watcher is per-manager (one `McpManager` instance in the extension) so no duplicate watchers per server.
- **Next item:** 1.101-6 · Chat UX improvements (distinct user messages, visible undo, navigable attachments).
